title: Incompatible Layout Assumptions on Cast Newtypes
pattern: Directly casting pointer addresses between a wrapper struct and its single underlying type, assuming identical memory layouts without representation annotation.
why_bad: Without representation attributes like `#[repr(transparent)]` or `#[repr(C)]`, the compiler does not guarantee that wrapper types share the same memory layout or alignment, causing unsafe raw pointer dereferences to read garbage or trigger segment faults.
detection: An unsafe raw pointer cast is performed between a generic single-field tuple struct (newtype) and its inner field type without standard representation annotations.
counterexample: Annotating the newtype with `#[repr(transparent)]` to guarantee identical layout and alignment.
fix: Apply the `#[repr(transparent)]` annotation to the wrapper struct definition.
